 Paste Function Help!
    Mason Earles <jmea...@ucdavis.edu> Nov 14 12:14PM -0800  

    Hi everyone--
     
    I'm trying to do something that I imagine is very simple with the paste
    function. Specifically, I need to paste several text strings together
    separated by commas. The catch is that I need each string to be surrounded
    by quotation marks. For instance,
     
    "blue" , "red" , "green"
     
    The function paste("blue" , "," , "red" "," "green") results in "blue , red
    , green". I believe this has to do with escape characters, but I can't
    figure it out.
     
    Thanks in advance!
    --Mason
     
     
    --
    Mason Earles
    PhD Student, Ecology Graduate Group
    University of California - Davis

     

    Noam Ross <noam...@gmail.com> Nov 14 12:24PM -0800  

    You can use single quotes as your "outer" quotes and doubles as your
    "inner", literal quotes:
     
    > a <- paste('"blue"','"red"','"green"')
    > a
    [1] "\"blue\" \"red\" \"green\""
    > cat(a)
    "blue" "red" "green"
     
    Note when you just type "a", this is equivalent to print(a), and this
    command adds the escape characters and quotes around the whole expression.
    cat(a), on the other hand, prints the exact expression.
     
     
    On Wed, Nov 14, 2012 at 12:14 PM, Mason Earles <jmea...@ucdavis.edu> wrote:
     

     

    Noam Ross <noam...@gmail.com> Nov 14 12:26PM -0800  

    Or, with commas:
     
    > a <- paste('"blue"','"red"','"green"', sep=",")
    > cat(a)
    "blue","red","green"

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: permutation ANOVA
parts:
I used `adonis` for "Permutational Multivariate Analysis of Variance Using Distance Ma- trices" from the `vegan` package, which I think might be the one you refer to in your question. 

To tell if it's what you need, you could check out the two papers by Marti Anderson that are referenced in the help page for that function.

-  Jaime
